messages.author: f24b6672b86b41b4
messages.subject: Segmentation fault with subread-align 1.5.0
parts:
Hi,

I am remapping my fastq files with the new 1.5.0 version of subread-align. Overall this has been successful. Out of a total of 2,664 fastq files, 2,356 ran without a problem. I am trying to figure out why the remaining files do not work with the latest version of Subread.

Here is how I ran subread-align v1.4.4 before. The input was a gzipped fastq, the output is bam. I only report uniquely mapping reads (-u) and use the Hamming distance to break ties (-H).

# Using version 1.4.4 with a genome indexed with buildindex from 1.4.4
subread-align -i $GENOME -r $FILE --gzFASTQinput --BAMoutput -uH > $OUTDIR/$BASE.bam

To obtain similar results with v1.5.0, I re-ran subread-buildindex and translated to the following for v1.5.0. The input is still a gzipped fastq and output bam. I still only report uniquely mapping reads, and the Hamming distance is used to break ties (at least according to the log sent to stderr. I assume this is now the only option since -H is no longer a flag).

# Using version 1.5.0 with a genome indexed with buildindex from 1.5.0
subread-align -i $GENOME -r $FILE -t 0 -u > $OUTDIR/$BASE.bam

So I guess first question is, did I translate this properly from v1.4.4 to v1.5.0?

I've created two test files to help isolate the problem. test-pass.fastq.gz works with both v1.4.4 and v1.5.0. test-fail.fastq.gz only works v1.4.4. Both test files contain 866,657 reads (3,466,628 lines). The reads in the two files are mutually-exclusive, but they are both subsets from the same sequencing run. The data is single end collected from humans. The reads have been quality trimmed, so they are varying lengths (20 bp <= length < 100 bp). I've placed them in my Dropbox Public folder for download:

https://www.dropbox.com/s/n20axbjlel8mhxz/test-pass.fastq.gz?dl=0
https://www.dropbox.com/s/b97f7otznmkzzfp/test-fail.fastq.gz?dl=0

I've attached the stderr from running test-fail.fastq.gz and test-pass.fastq.gz using either v1.4.4 or v1.5.0. These were run sequentially on the same compute node with 12g of RAM.

I checked to see if there was a difference in the number of very short reads (20 bp), but there is not a substantial difference between the two test files.

Can you identify what is causing the segmentation fault? Please let me know if there is any other information you would like me to provide.

Thanks,

John

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: Segmentation fault with subread-align 1.5.0
parts:
Hi John,

Many thanks for providing the data. We found that the seg fault was caused by a bug in implementing a new function for reading in gzipped fastq files in version 1.5.0 (1.5.0 processes gzipped fastq files more efficiently than previous versions). We have fixed this bug and are working on releasing a patched version this week.

Cheers,
Wei
